Repligen beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $204.1 million, up 11.9% year on year. It was a very strong quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates and a solid beat of analysts’ organic revenue estimates.
Is Repligen a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Repligen’s revenue to grow 9.6% year on year, slowing from the 21.9% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Repligen rarely misses Wall Street’s revenue estimates.

Looking at Repligen’s peers in the life sciences tools & services segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Medpace delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 8.5%, meeting analysts’ expectations, and Thermo Fisher reported revenues up 9.1%, topping estimates by 1.4%. Medpace traded down 1.5% following the results while Thermo Fisher was also down 1.6%.

There has been positive sentiment among investors in the life sciences tools & services segment, with share prices up 2.7% on average over the last month. Repligen is down 8.8% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $201.45 (compared to the current share price of $177.03).
